Comment: The paper reports the mean difference as 2.1 with a 95% CI of 2.0-2.2, which is implausibly narrow given SDs of 2.5 and 2.1 with n=30 per arm; the CI bounds were therefore NOT recorded. Original drug/unit: intravenous morphine in mg; conversion factor 3 recorded for IV morphine -> oral morphine equivalents (2.9 mg IV = 8.7 mg OME; 5.0 mg IV = 15.0 mg OME) - conversion not applied to the stored means/SDs by the extractor.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group B (block group): ultrasound-guided ESPB at T5, ropivacaine 0.5%, 0.4 mL/kg') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized controlled trial, parallel two-arm, between-subjects
Participant type: Adult female patients (ASA I-II, aged 18-60) undergoing total mastectomy and axillary clearance under general anaesthesia
Recruitment source: Single tertiary care centre (PGIMER, Chandigarh, India), July 2017-December 2018
Outcome measurement: Mean (SD) milligrams of intravenous morphine consumed over the first 24 postoperative hours, recorded from the PCA device
outcome_family: cumulative 24-hour postoperative opioid consumption (oral morphine equivalents, mg)
effect_direction: favours ESPB (2.9 vs 5.0 mg IV morphine)
